newsitem.title: UK: London gold holds gains at fix post jobs data.
newsitem.headline: London gold holds gains at fix post jobs data.

text.p: The price of gold was supported by U.S. jobs data and speculation on a U.S. interest rate hike on Friday it had managed to recover some of the losses suffered in a dramatic New Year slide. Gold blipped on the payroll figures before a London afternoon fix at $358.25 per ounce. Although down 30 cents from the morning, this was $1.75 ahead from Thursday afternoon.
"The market is finally showing a spark of life. If we're able to close around $360 today, it will augur well for gold next week," one dealer said.
Gold's rise from fresh 3-1/4 year lows below $354 an ounce on Thursday was on shortcovering and Japanese buying.

The December U.S. nonfarm payrolls increased 262,000 from an upwardly revised November figure and economists' forecasts averaging 192,000. The jobless rate was unchanged and matched forecasts at 5.3 percent.

Some bullion analysts said there was an increasing chance that the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) which meets February 4 and 5 would propose a rise in U.S. interest rates to the Federal Reserve Board (central bank). "There is talk that the FOMC might suggest a rise next month. But what happens to gold would depend on the reaction of the stock and bonds markets where a big correction would be needed to help gold," one analyst said.
Friday's Japanese buying was in reaction to a falling dollar/yen and a sharp drop in the Tokyo stock market. Unusually the rise was not sold into by Australian producers.
Gold could expect stiff nearby $360 resistance, dealers and analysts added, and above that a surge to $365 next week was possible if there were no significant technical resistance.
But the tone was still bearish. "Gold isn't looking strong. There's no reason for investment funds to take their profits yet," one dealer said.
Gold could test the important $345-$343 support area this month, several analysts said.
Silver was indicated three cents firmer at $4.73/$4.75,just of its intraday high after ticking up with gold.
Platinum firmed on dealer buying to be $3.70 up at $463.70/$364.70.
Palladium was $1.75 ahead at $122.00/$123.00 on concerns over Russian supplies.
